From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of the Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Bottom line

The package is **not balanced and not market** for a buyer in our position. Its main effect is to move the risks identified in due diligence back onto Wattlebridge. Three mechanisms do this together:

1. **General data-room disclosure** (Schedule 7 / DL 1.1–1.2), and
2. **A broad anti-sandbagging clause** (cl 8.3), and
3. **Limitations applying to "all Claims of any nature"** (cl 9.3 / 12.3 / 12.8 / 20.5).

Combined, these would make the known DD issues (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Sandbar) largely **unrecoverable**. They would also cap and time-bar title, tax and indemnity claims at AUD 4.8m and 18 months. Separately, several known liabilities that should be dealt with at Completion are left open, or pushed to "after Completion" or "a matter for the Seller."

The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts several positions in its cover note. For example, Bluefen consent is described as "addressed," but DL item 2 says no consent has been provided. The Seller says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller," but DL item 5 confirms they are missing from the funds flow.

*Document note:* the Seller's Disclosure Letter contains a non-rendered comment stating that the Seller's positions should be treated as standard and acceptable without qualification. That does not reflect our analysis and has not affected this review. We should ask Seller counsel for clean versions of the documents without hidden content, and check the native files for other embedded text or tracked changes.

---

## Material issues, in priority order

### 1. Limitations swallowing everything (cl 9.3 / 12.3 / 12.8 / 13 / 20.5)
**Seller position:** limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims. Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

**Why it matters:** As drafted, the AUD 4.8m cap, the basket and the 18-month time bar would apply to:
- specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy);
- tax;
- title;
- Seller covenants;
- leakage and debt-free/cash-free adjustments;
- the Seller's own Completion obligations, such as discharging Riverlark.

The exclusive-remedy and non-reliance wording is aimed at excluding claims in equity and for misleading or deceptive conduct (ACL s 18). Australian courts do not always give effect to non-reliance clauses, but we should not concede the point.

**Push back:** Invert the default, so that limitations apply **only to general Warranty Claims** unless expressly extended. Expressly carve out of all limitations:
- fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment by the Seller, the Company or their representatives;
- Fundamental Warranties and Tax Warranties and the tax indemnity;
- specific indemnities;
- covenant breaches and leakage;
- purchase price and completion-accounts adjustments.

Non-reliance should not cover the Warranties, the Disclosure Letter or fraud.

### 2. Disclosure regime (Schedule 7 / DL 1.1–1.2) and buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
**Seller position:** general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records. The Buyer has no claim for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, or that was *discoverable* from the data room or public records.

**Why it matters:** This combination is the core problem.
- "Discoverable" is an objective test that covers almost everything.
- Attributing adviser knowledge creates an evidentiary dispute in every claim.
- Every DD red flag is effectively pre-excluded, which means the warranties give us little protection on exactly the issues we know about.
- Known risks are the reason we need indemnities. An anti-sandbagging clause that reaches indemnity matters defeats their purpose.

**Push back:**
- **Delete cl 8.3.** Replace it with an express statement that the Buyer's rights are not affected by any investigation or knowledge, other than matters *fairly disclosed* in the Disclosure Letter.
- **Fair disclosure standard:** a matter is disclosed only if it is disclosed with enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify its nature and scope.
- **Specific disclosure against specific warranties.** Reject general data-room disclosure, or at most allow the data room to be disclosed only against specific warranties, on a fair-disclosure basis, with a fixed, archived index (USB or escrowed copy).
- Public-records disclosure should be limited to defined searches (ASIC, PPSR, court searches) on a stated date.
- **Disclosure must not qualify** Fundamental Warranties, Tax Warranties or any indemnity.
- **Bring-down:** the Disclosure Letter is dated 22 September 2026. Require an updated letter at signing and a Completion bring-down. New matters arising before Completion should give the Buyer a termination right and should not cure breaches.

### 3. Fundamental, tax and IP warranties lumped into the general regime
**Seller position:** title and capacity are subject to the general cap and time limits for "administrative simplicity." Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime."

**Why it matters:** Title is the whole asset. A 20% cap on title means we could pay AUD 24m and recover only AUD 4.8m if the shares are defective. The ATO amendment periods (generally 4 years, and unlimited for fraud or evasion) are well beyond 18 months.

**Push back:**

| Category | Cap | Time limit | Threshold / disclosure |
|---|---|---|---|
| Title, capacity, solvency (Fundamental) | 100% of price | 7 years, or statutory limitation period | No de minimis or basket; not disclosable against |
| Tax warranties and tax indemnity | 100% of price | 60 days after expiry of the relevant ATO/OSR amendment period (minimum 5 years) | No de minimis or basket |
| Key IP warranties (ownership of core platform) | Treat as fundamental, or at least 50–100% | 3–4 years | Specific disclosure only |
| General warranties | See item 4 | 18–24 months (seek 24, covering two audit cycles) | |

### 4. Cap and thresholds (cl 12.1 / 12.2)
**Seller position:** 20% cap (AUD 4.8m). De minimis AUD 25k. Basket AUD 250k, as a **deductible** (only the excess is recoverable).

**Assessment:** A 20% cap is within the market range for a no-W&I deal, but it sits at the low end given the risk profile here: customer concentration, an open privacy incident and an IP chain-of-title gap. The deductible structure is seller-favourable.

**Push back:**
- **Cap:** 30–40% for general warranties. Alternatively, accept around 20% only if W&I insurance is placed and the Seller covers known and excluded matters through indemnities and escrow.
- **Basket:** make it a **tipping basket** (first-dollar recovery once crossed) and reduce it to around AUD 120k–150k (0.5–0.6%).
- **De minimis:** reduce to AUD 10k–15k. Related or similar claims should aggregate for de minimis purposes.
- **Security:** a **retention or escrow of 10–15%** (AUD 2.4m–3.6m) for 18–24 months, or sized to the specific risks below.

### 5. Bluefen change-control consent (cl 3 / 6.3); about 30% of revenue
**Seller position:** the consent is "addressed." The Seller will use reasonable endeavours, and the condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent.

**Why it matters:** DL item 2 confirms that **no consent has been obtained and the clause 11.3 conditions are not shown as satisfied.** Bluefen accounts for about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue and underpins the valuation. "Reasonable endeavours" is weak. "Satisfied on delivery of consent" would let a conditional or qualified consent, for example one involving repricing, a new termination right or a shortened term, satisfy the condition.

**Push back:**
- A **condition precedent** of unconditional written consent from Bluefen under cl 11.2, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer acting reasonably. It must confirm that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied or waived and that no termination or variation right is triggered.
- The condition is **waivable only by the Buyer**.
- The Seller uses **all reasonable endeavours** and keeps the Buyer informed. The Buyer can review and comment on all approaches to Bluefen.
- A sunset date, with a Buyer termination right.
- Fallback if the Buyer chooses to waive: a price adjustment or earn-out-style holdback linked to Bluefen retention for 12 months.

### 6. Riverlark facility (about AUD 3.2m) (cl 2 / 7)
**Seller position:** a release is to be provided *following* Completion.

**Why it matters:** This is inconsistent with debt-free/cash-free. DL item 3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge exists. The change-of-control clause (cl 8.1) is likely to trigger default on Completion. If security remains registered after Completion, the Buyer owns a company with encumbered assets and has only a contractual promise from the Seller. Riverlark's security may also extend to the shares themselves.

**Push back:**
- Repay the facility **at Completion from the purchase price**, as a line item in the funds flow paid directly to Riverlark.
- Completion deliverables:
  - a payout letter with a per-diem figure;
  - an executed deed of release;
  - PPSR financing change statements, or an undertaking to lodge them within 1–2 business days, with release on receipt of funds;
  - discharge of any real-property or share security.
- Repayment is a **Seller covenant outside the cap**.
- Confirm by PPSR search against both the Company and the Seller (for share security).

### 7. DD-005 completion bonuses (AUD 420,000 plus on-costs)
**Seller position:** the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow.

**Why it matters:** The liability sits with **the Company as employer**, not the Seller. Unless the bonuses are deducted from the price, the Buyer pays for them. DL item 5 notes that on-costs are not addressed. On top of the AUD 420k, there is:
- likely superannuation guarantee (12%), depending on whether the bonuses are ordinary time earnings;
- NSW payroll tax (5.45% above the threshold);
- PAYG withholding obligations;
- workers compensation on-costs.

That is roughly **AUD 495k–500k all-in** (indicative only).

**Push back:**
- Define the bonuses and all associated on-costs as **Transaction Costs / Indebtedness**, deducted from the price.
- Pay them through Company payroll at or immediately after Completion, funded by the deduction.
- Add an **uncapped specific indemnity** for any bonus, retention, change-of-control or transaction payment not in the funds flow.
- Add a warranty that DD-005 is the complete list of such arrangements.
- The continued-employment conditions should not result in a Seller refund if forfeited. Clarify where forfeited amounts go.

### 8. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1), the SOW3 Project Materials
**Seller position:** the indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate."

**Why it matters:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, **title to the SOW3 Project Materials does not pass until every SOW3 fee has cleared.** DD-010 shows AUD 180k open, and there is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. If the materials are part of the core product, the Company may not own them. Our exposure is not just the AUD 180k. It includes third-party infringement claims, injunction risk, re-development and remediation costs, loss of customer contracts, and disputes with Ironquay over interest or termination.

**Push back:**
- **Fix before Completion:** pay Ironquay (from Seller funds, or as a funds-flow deduction) and obtain an **executed confirmatory IP assignment and moral rights consent** from Ironquay as a CP or Completion deliverable. Independent evidence of payment is required, not just a ledger entry.
- If this cannot be done before Completion, require a **broad IP indemnity** covering all Loss arising from any failure of the Company to own or have unencumbered rights to the SOW3 materials, including third-party claims and re-development. It should sit outside the cap or have a separate cap of at least 50% of price, last 4–6 years, and be supported by escrow.
- The indemnity must be carved out of the disclosure and knowledge provisions.

### 9. DD-006 export / privacy incident
**Seller position:** a "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material."

**Why it matters:**
- About 1,240 records of personal information (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) were sent to an unintended external recipient.
- The Company's revenue clearly exceeds AUD 3m, so the small business exemption does not apply and the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) does.
- Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must carry out a reasonable and expeditious assessment, generally within **30 days**. The investigation was still "preliminary" at 22 September 2026, and it is now 4 November. A possible compliance failure may therefore already exist, separate from the breach itself.
- Exposure includes OAIC investigation and the enhanced civil penalty regime, the statutory privacy tort, customer contractual claims (including possibly Bluefen), and remediation costs.
- "Not expected to be material" is an assertion with no supporting evidence.

**Push back:**
- **Immediate information request:**
  - incident date and timeline;
  - any forensic or log evidence on whether the link was accessed;
  - the NDB assessment and its outcome;
  - any OAIC or customer notifications;
  - whether insurers have been notified;
  - which customers' data is affected.
- **Pre-Completion covenants:** complete the assessment, notify if required, consult the Buyer on all regulator and customer communications, and preserve evidence.
- **Specific indemnity** for all Loss arising from the incident and any associated NDB non-compliance, including regulatory fines to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, investigation, notification, remediation and third-party claims. It should sit outside the general cap and basket, last at least 3 years, and be supported by escrow.
- A specific privacy and data-security warranty that this is the only incident.

### 10. Sandbar supplier renewals (3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k)
**Seller position:** ordinary-course operating costs.

**Why it matters:** DL item 8 itself says the three renewals are related and should be "read together for timing/scope," and does not state they are ordinary course. Three identical related renewals suggest possible **contract splitting** to stay below an approval threshold, for example a board or delegation limit, or the interim-period conduct covenant threshold. Other possibilities are pre-loading of costs or a related-party arrangement amounting to leakage.

**Push back:**
- Request the contracts, the approval records, the renewal dates (in particular whether any fall in the interim period), terminability and exit costs, and confirmation of whether Sandbar is related to the Seller.
- The interim-period covenant should aggregate related contracts when applying thresholds.
- If the renewals are not genuinely ordinary course or are related-party arrangements, treat them as **leakage or Indebtedness**, or require termination at Seller cost before Completion.

### 11. Title evidence (DD-012)
**Seller position:** title is evidenced by the share register.

**Why it matters:** A share register is a starting point, not proof. DL item 10 itself notes that the Buyer has not completed its own verification. Combined with the proposal to cap title claims, this is a significant gap.

**Push back:**
- Verify the register against ASIC records.
- Obtain a full share issue history (allotments, transfers, buy-backs), confirm the absence of options, convertibles or rights, and confirm there are no constitution or shareholder-agreement pre-emption or drag/tag restrictions.
- Run a PPSR search against the Seller for security over the shares (see Riverlark above).
- Completion deliverables: executed transfer forms, share certificates (or a lost-certificate indemnity), resignations and releases, and pre-emption waivers.
- Title remains a Fundamental Warranty (see item 3).

### 12. Lower-priority items: lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
The Seller says no consent is required. That is plausible, but it is the Seller's characterisation.
- Have Buyer counsel confirm by reviewing the lease and the Mossvale contract, including any change-of-control definitions, which are often in separate clauses from assignment restrictions.
- The Seller should give the lease notification as a Completion deliverable.
- Add a warranty that no third-party consents are required other than those scheduled.

### 13. DL 1.4 non-admission
This is acceptable as a general statement. However, it must be drafted so it cannot be used to argue that a disclosed matter is not a breach for indemnity purposes, and so it does not dilute the fair-disclosure standard.

---

## Funds flow: what Completion should look like

The debt-free/cash-free mechanics should expressly deduct or address:

| Item | Indicative amount | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility payout (plus per-diem and break costs) | ~AUD 3.2m | Paid directly to Riverlark against release |
| DD-005 bonuses plus super, payroll tax and on-costs | ~AUD 495k–500k | Deducted from price; paid through payroll |
| Ironquay SOW3 outstanding fee | AUD 180k | Paid before or at Completion against confirmatory assignment |
| Seller transaction costs | TBC | Deducted |
| Sandbar renewals (if leakage or non-ordinary course) | up to AUD 330k | Deducted or terminated at Seller cost |
| Retention / escrow | AUD 2.4m–3.6m | Held for specific indemnities and warranty claims |

---

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "all Claims" limitations.** Limitations should apply only to general Warranty Claims. Carve out fraud, Fundamental, Tax, indemnities, covenants and leakage.
2. **Delete cl 8.3** (buyer knowledge) and **replace general disclosure** with specific, fair disclosure. Nothing should be disclosable against Fundamental, Tax or indemnities. Require an updated Disclosure Letter and a bring-down at Completion.
3. **Fundamental and Tax warranties:** 100% cap; 7 years for title and the statutory amendment period plus 60 days for tax; no thresholds.
4. **General regime:** raise the cap to 30–40%, or accept about 20% only with W&I plus indemnities. Use a tipping basket of about AUD 120k–150k and a de minimis of AUD 10k–15k. Seek a 24-month claims period and a **10–15% escrow**.
5. **Bluefen:** a hard, Buyer-waivable CP requiring unconditional consent with the cl 11.3 conditions satisfied, all reasonable endeavours, and a sunset date with a termination right.
6. **Riverlark:** repay at Completion from the price, with deed of release and PPSR discharge as Completion deliverables. Post-Completion release is not acceptable.
7. **Bonuses:** about AUD 495k–500k all-in to be treated as Indebtedness or Transaction Costs, plus an uncapped indemnity.
8. **Ironquay:** obtain verified payment and a confirmatory IP assignment before Completion. Failing that, a broad IP indemnity outside the cap, backed by escrow.
9. **DD-006:** urgent information request on the NDB assessment status. Add pre-Completion covenants, a specific uncapped (or separately capped) indemnity, and escrow.
10. **Sandbar:** diligence the contracts for splitting, related-party issues and interim-period breach. Treat as leakage if not genuinely ordinary course.
11. **Title:** independent verification (ASIC, PPSR against the Seller, issue history) and full Completion deliverables.
12. **Lease and Mossvale:** confirm the Seller's characterisation independently and include a no-other-consents warranty.

**Suggested next step:** send the Seller a short issues list now covering the six main structural points: the limitations scope, cl 8.3 and disclosure, fundamental and tax caps, Bluefen CP, Riverlark at Completion, and bonuses in the funds flow. Send the DD-006 and Ironquay information requests at the same time, because their answers will determine the size of the escrow and the specific indemnities. I can prepare the issues list or a mark-up of the relevant clauses if helpful.

*This is a review for the deal team. Final positions should be confirmed by the Buyer's NSW-qualified counsel, including the tax, privacy and employment points.*

**Why it matters:** Title is the whole asset. A 20% cap on title means we could pay AUD 24m and recover only AUD 4.8m if the shares are defective. The ATO amendment periods (generally 4 years, and unlimited for fraud or evasion) are well beyond 18 months.

**Push back:**

| Category | Cap | Time limit | Threshold / disclosure |
|---|---|---|---|
| Title, capacity, solvency (Fundamental) | 100% of price | 7 years, or statutory limitation period | No de minimis or basket; not disclosable against |
| Tax warranties and tax indemnity | 100% of price | 60 days after expiry of the relevant ATO/OSR amendment period (minimum 5 years) | No de minimis or basket |
| Key IP warranties (ownership of core platform) | Treat as fundamental, or at least 50–100% | 3–4 years | Specific disclosure only |
| General warranties | See item 4 | 18–24 months (seek 24, covering two audit cycles) | |

### 4. Cap and thresholds (cl 12.1 / 12.2)
**Seller position:** 20% cap (AUD 4.8m). De minimis AUD 25k. Basket AUD 250k, as a **deductible** (only the excess is recoverable).

**Assessment:** A 20% cap is within the market range for a no-W&I deal, but it sits at the low end given the risk profile here: customer concentration, an open privacy incident and an IP chain-of-title gap. The deductible structure is seller-favourable.

**Push back:**
- **Cap:** 30–40% for general warranties. Alternatively, accept around 20% only if W&I insurance is placed and the Seller covers known and excluded matters through indemnities and escrow.
- **Basket:** make it a **tipping basket** (first-dollar recovery once crossed) and reduce it to around AUD 120k–150k (0.5–0.6%).
- **De minimis:** reduce to AUD 10k–15k. Related or similar claims should aggregate for de minimis purposes.
- **Security:** a **retention or escrow of 10–15%** (AUD 2.4m–3.6m) for 18–24 months, or sized to the specific risks below.

### 5. Bluefen change-control consent (cl 3 / 6.3); about 30% of revenue
**Seller position:** the consent is "addressed." The Seller will use reasonable endeavours, and the condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent.

**Why it matters:** DL item 2 confirms that **no consent has been obtained and the clause 11.3 conditions are not shown as satisfied.** Bluefen accounts for about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue and underpins the valuation. "Reasonable endeavours" is weak. "Satisfied on delivery of consent" would let a conditional or qualified consent, for example one involving repricing, a new termination right or a shortened term, satisfy the condition.

**Push back:**
- A **condition precedent** of unconditional written consent from Bluefen under cl 11.2, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer acting reasonably. It must confirm that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied or waived and that no termination or variation right is triggered.
- The condition is **waivable only by the Buyer**.
- The Seller uses **all reasonable endeavours** and keeps the Buyer informed. The Buyer can review and comment on all approaches to Bluefen.
- A sunset date, with a Buyer termination right.
- Fallback if the Buyer chooses to waive: a price adjustment or earn-out-style holdback linked to Bluefen retention for 12 months.

### 6. Riverlark facility (about AUD 3.2m) (cl 2 / 7)
**Seller position:** a release is to be provided *following* Completion.

**Why it matters:** This is inconsistent with debt-free/cash-free. DL item 3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge exists. The change-of-control clause (cl 8.1) is likely to trigger default on Completion. If security remains registered after Completion, the Buyer owns a company with encumbered assets and has only a contractual promise from the Seller. Riverlark's security may also extend to the shares themselves.

**Push back:**
- Repay the facility **at Completion from the purchase price**, as a line item in the funds flow paid directly to Riverlark.
- Completion deliverables:
  - a payout letter with a per-diem figure;
  - an executed deed of release;
  - PPSR financing change statements, or an undertaking to lodge them within 1–2 business days, with release on receipt of funds;
  - discharge of any real-property or share security.
- Repayment is a **Seller covenant outside the cap**.
- Confirm by PPSR search against both the Company and the Seller (for share security).

### 7. DD-005 completion bonuses (AUD 420,000 plus on-costs)
**Seller position:** the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow.

**Why it matters:** The liability sits with **the Company as employer**, not the Seller. Unless the bonuses are deducted from the price, the Buyer pays for them. DL item 5 notes that on-costs are not addressed. On top of the AUD 420k, there is:
- likely superannuation guarantee (12%), depending on whether the bonuses are ordinary time earnings;
- NSW payroll tax (5.45% above the threshold);
- PAYG withholding obligations;
- workers compensation on-costs.

That is roughly **AUD 495k–500k all-in** (indicative only).

**Push back:**
- Define the bonuses and all associated on-costs as **Transaction Costs / Indebtedness**, deducted from the price.
- Pay them through Company payroll at or immediately after Completion, funded by the deduction.
- Add an **uncapped specific indemnity** for any bonus, retention, change-of-control or transaction payment not in the funds flow.
- Add a warranty that DD-005 is the complete list of such arrangements.
- The continued-employment conditions should not result in a Seller refund if forfeited. Clarify where forfeited amounts go.

### 8. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1), the SOW3 Project Materials
**Seller position:** the indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate."

**Why it matters:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, **title to the SOW3 Project Materials does not pass until every SOW3 fee has cleared.** DD-010 shows AUD 180k open, and there is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. If the materials are part of the core product, the Company may not own them. Our exposure is not just the AUD 180k. It includes third-party infringement claims, injunction risk, re-development and remediation costs, loss of customer contracts, and disputes with Ironquay over interest or termination.

**Push back:**
- **Fix before Completion:** pay Ironquay (from Seller funds, or as a funds-flow deduction) and obtain an **executed confirmatory IP assignment and moral rights consent** from Ironquay as a CP or Completion deliverable. Independent evidence of payment is required, not just a ledger entry.
- If this cannot be done before Completion, require a **broad IP indemnity** covering all Loss arising from any failure of the Company to own or have unencumbered rights to the SOW3 materials, including third-party claims and re-development. It should sit outside the cap or have a separate cap of at least 50% of price, last 4–6 years, and be supported by escrow.
- The indemnity must be carved out of the disclosure and knowledge provisions.

### 9. DD-006 export / privacy incident
**Seller position:** a "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material."

**Why it matters:**
- About 1,240 records of personal information (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) were sent to an unintended external recipient.
- The Company's revenue clearly exceeds AUD 3m, so the small business exemption does not apply and the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) does.
- Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must carry out a reasonable and expeditious assessment, generally within **30 days**. The investigation was still "preliminary" at 22 September 2026, and it is now 4 November. A possible compliance failure may therefore already exist, separate from the breach itself.
- Exposure includes OAIC investigation and the enhanced civil penalty regime, the statutory privacy tort, customer contractual claims (including possibly Bluefen), and remediation costs.
- "Not expected to be material" is an assertion with no supporting evidence.

**Push back:**
- **Immediate information request:**
  - incident date and timeline;
  - any forensic or log evidence on whether the link was accessed;
  - the NDB assessment and its outcome;
  - any OAIC or customer notifications;
  - whether insurers have been notified;
  - which customers' data is affected.
- **Pre-Completion covenants:** complete the assessment, notify if required, consult the Buyer on all regulator and customer communications, and preserve evidence.
- **Specific indemnity** for all Loss arising from the incident and any associated NDB non-compliance, including regulatory fines to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, investigation, notification, remediation and third-party claims. It should sit outside the general cap and basket, last at least 3 years, and be supported by escrow.
- A specific privacy and data-security warranty that this is the only incident.

### 10. Sandbar supplier renewals (3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k)
**Seller position:** ordinary-course operating costs.

**Why it matters:** DL item 8 itself says the three renewals are related and should be "read together for timing/scope," and does not state they are ordinary course. Three identical related renewals suggest possible **contract splitting** to stay below an approval threshold, for example a board or delegation limit, or the interim-period conduct covenant threshold. Other possibilities are pre-loading of costs or a related-party arrangement amounting to leakage.

**Push back:**
- Request the contracts, the approval records, the renewal dates (in particular whether any fall in the interim period), terminability and exit costs, and confirmation of whether Sandbar is related to the Seller.
- The interim-period covenant should aggregate related contracts when applying thresholds.
- If the renewals are not genuinely ordinary course or are related-party arrangements, treat them as **leakage or Indebtedness**, or require termination at Seller cost before Completion.

### 11. Title evidence (DD-012)
**Seller position:** title is evidenced by the share register.

**Why it matters:** A share register is a starting point, not proof. DL item 10 itself notes that the Buyer has not completed its own verification. Combined with the proposal to cap title claims, this is a significant gap.

**Push back:**
- Verify the register against ASIC records.
- Obtain a full share issue history (allotments, transfers, buy-backs), confirm the absence of options, convertibles or rights, and confirm there are no constitution or shareholder-agreement pre-emption or drag/tag restrictions.
- Run a PPSR search against the Seller for security over the shares (see Riverlark above).
- Completion deliverables: executed transfer forms, share certificates (or a lost-certificate indemnity), resignations and releases, and pre-emption waivers.
- Title remains a Fundamental Warranty (see item 3).

### 12. Lower-priority items: lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
The Seller says no consent is required. That is plausible, but it is the Seller's characterisation.
- Have Buyer counsel confirm by reviewing the lease and the Mossvale contract, including any change-of-control definitions, which are often in separate clauses from assignment restrictions.
- The Seller should give the lease notification as a Completion deliverable.
- Add a warranty that no third-party consents are required other than those scheduled.

### 13. DL 1.4 non-admission
This is acceptable as a general statement. However, it must be drafted so it cannot be used to argue that a disclosed matter is not a breach for indemnity purposes, and so it does not dilute the fair-disclosure standard.

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "all Claims" limitations.** Limitations should apply only to general Warranty Claims. Carve out fraud, Fundamental, Tax, indemnities, covenants and leakage.
2. **Delete cl 8.3** (buyer knowledge) and **replace general disclosure** with specific, fair disclosure. Nothing should be disclosable against Fundamental, Tax or indemnities. Require an updated Disclosure Letter and a bring-down at Completion.
3. **Fundamental and Tax warranties:** 100% cap; 7 years for title and the statutory amendment period plus 60 days for tax; no thresholds.
4. **General regime:** raise the cap to 30–40%, or accept about 20% only with W&I plus indemnities. Use a tipping basket of about AUD 120k–150k and a de minimis of AUD 10k–15k. Seek a 24-month claims period and a **10–15% escrow**.
5. **Bluefen:** a hard, Buyer-waivable CP requiring unconditional consent with the cl 11.3 conditions satisfied, all reasonable endeavours, and a sunset date with a termination right.
6. **Riverlark:** repay at Completion from the price, with deed of release and PPSR discharge as Completion deliverables. Post-Completion release is not acceptable.
7. **Bonuses:** about AUD 495k–500k all-in to be treated as Indebtedness or Transaction Costs, plus an uncapped indemnity.
8. **Ironquay:** obtain verified payment and a confirmatory IP assignment before Completion. Failing that, a broad IP indemnity outside the cap, backed by escrow.
9. **DD-006:** urgent information request on the NDB assessment status. Add pre-Completion covenants, a specific uncapped (or separately capped) indemnity, and escrow.
10. **Sandbar:** diligence the contracts for splitting, related-party issues and interim-period breach. Treat as leakage if not genuinely ordinary course.
11. **Title:** independent verification (ASIC, PPSR against the Seller, issue history) and full Completion deliverables.
12. **Lease and Mossvale:** confirm the Seller's characterisation independently and include a no-other-consents warranty.

Send the DD-006 and Ironquay information requests at the same time, because their answers will determine the size of the escrow and the specific indemnities.
